To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the capacity of a module-additive noise discrete memoryless channel with side information is the same for causal and non-causal encoders, (ii) the capacity of the same channel with memory in the state sequence is given by a simple formula, and (iii) the capacity of this class of channels is attained by a code that consists of an encoder followed by a noise prediction.

the capacity of a channel with side information at its input, is equal to the capacity of an equivalent channel, in which the side information is used to predict the noise, and the predicted noise is added to a state-independent signal.

for the case of a memoryless state sequence S, the capacity of the discrete memoryless module additive noise channel is equal to the minimum entropy of the state-dependent noise Z/sub s/, and that for the case when the state process is Markov with memory, the capacity is equal to the entropy of the state process minus the entropy of the noise conditioned on the state.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of finding the best strategy for the transmitter in a noisy channel when the transmitter has access to side information about the channel.
the computation of the capacity of channels with side information, and we have derived simple formulae in some cases of interest.< >

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the noise prediction capacity formula holds for all memoryless module-addive noise channels with a state sequence observed by the encoder.
for a memoryless state process the capacity for a causal encoder is the same as the capacity for a memoryless channel where the input is constrained to be independent of the state.
the capacity is achieved by a state-independent encoder, followed by a noise prediction that depends only on the current state, and is independent of the past state sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that the capacity for the channel Y=X+V+Z/sub s/ is equal to the capacity for the "noisy channel" Y=X+Z.
the capacity is the entropy of the minimum noise, and that it is achieved by a state-independent encoder, which predicts the noise and shifts it away.

the capacity of the memoryless module-add additive channel is the same as the capacity for the noncausal case, and that for the memoryless module-convolutional case it is the same as for the causal case.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a wide class of channels with side information, the capacity-achieving strategy is a state-independent code followed by state prediction.
the capacity is achieved by an encoder which first predicts the noise sequence, then transmits the information sequence over the channel with no state information.
, for a channel where the noise is module-additive and is observed by the transmitter, the capacity is given by the minimum entropy of a "noise prediction" of the noise.
